answer: Hypothesis: The highest growth phase within 2000–1100 BCE occurred in the 15th and 14th centuries BCE (1500–1400 BCE). The 15th century BCE has the highest mean growth rate of the 100-year smoothed pollen openness score (pollen_grate_100 mean +0.00189/yr; median +0.00174; max +0.00465), followed by the 14th century BCE (+0.00111 mean). The evidence indicates a plateau-like growth phase spanning these two adjacent centuries rather than one single dominant century: the two centuries swap ranks depending on the exact growth definition (pollen_grate_100 and the diff of pollen_inter_100 favor 1500 BCE; the recomputed diff of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y favors 1400 BCE), while the archaeological KDE growth rate (g_all_mean) peaks at 1500 BCE (+0.00283) with 1400 BCE second (+0.00145), and the capital indicators show their strongest century-over-century jump at 1400 BCE (composite Z +0.68, driven by CopperGold 0.03→2.54 and MonumentCount −0.82→+1.71 during the OBA phase). Corroborating (not merged) corroboration detail: 1700 BCE is a distant third on pollen_grate_100 (+0.00086); all other centuries are flat or negative, and 1600 BCE is the strongest decline (−0.00301) immediately preceding the growth phase. Caveat: because growth is measured on a 100-year smoothed openness series, growth peaks lead the openness-level peak — the smoothed openness level itself reaches its century-mean maximum at 1300 BCE (2.49) — so the 15th–14th-century BCE growth phase is the ascent that culminates in the 13th-century BCE openness maximum. No corroboration source contradicts the pollen-growth ranking of the top centuries; the only disagreement is the internal ordering of the 1500-vs-1400 pair across growth definitions.

payload.workflow: Loaded the three CSVs (comma-decimal handling for capital.csv and the pollen file); confirmed time axes (CE + calBP = 1950). Restricted time_series_data.csv to CE −2000…−1100 (901 annual rows), binned into BCE centuries (century c = CE [−c, −c+99]), and computed mean/median/max of pollen_grate_100 per century with a boundary-year (CE −1100) sensitivity check. Corroborated with per-century g_all_mean, century-mean levels and deltas of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y and pollen_inter_100, and capital.csv Z-columns (per-column and composite, with century-over-century deltas). Ran a recomputed-growth sensitivity analysis using first differences of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y and pollen_inter_100 plus 100-y cumulative smoothed-level change. All ranking results and diagnostics are in analysis/results_growth_phase.txt; script in analysis/analysis_growth_phase.py.
